text:
Anya W: Heads up — customer hit a blocker bootstrapping the JS SDK in a Next+Edge sample. Build works in Node but the edge bundle fails at runtime. Probable combo: ESM/CJS entrypoints + TS generics + overloads. Anyone seen weird overload resolution that only shows up after swc/rollup?

Matt R: ugh yeah. bundlers can rewrite exports and that ends up picking the wrong entry. do we have a repro?

Anya W: Minimal repro attached inline. It passes tsc locally but in edge it throws: "TypeError: client.create is not a function". Likely an export interop issue plus an overload inference mismatch.

Jordan P: can you paste the overloads? 99% it's the generic inference fallback to 'any' vs 'unknown' and then an overload with 'any' matches at runtime after transpile. super subtle.

Anya W: here it is:

```ts
// sdk/api.ts (source)
export function createClient<T>(opts: { auth: string }): Client<T>;
export function createClient(opts: { auth?: string }): Client<any> {
  // runtime impl
  return new Client(opts.auth);
}

// consumer.ts
const client = createClient<{ user: { id: string } }>({ auth: process.env.TOK });
client.create({ user: { id: '123' } }) // runtime: OK in Node, fails in edge bundle
```

Jordan P: yep — bundler/tsc can erase the explicit generic in some fast-path builds, then overload resolution picks the non-generic overload. If the ESM build exports get rewritten to a default+named shim, consumer ends up calling wrong fn.

Sasha L: two angles: 1) SDK entry/export surface: ensure the ESM entrypoint exports exact same named shapes (avoid dual default shims). 2) TS surface: prefer a single signature with constrained generic or use a generic with explicit default to avoid overloads.

Sasha L: recommended tsconfig for edge-friendly builds (we use SWC but tsc sanity):

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": true
  }
}
```

Matt R: also check package.json "exports" map. If you have both "require" and "import" targets, some bundlers will pick an unexpected subpath. For edge we ship only esm entry under "exports" for dist/edge.

Matt R: quick workaround in SDK code: collapse overloads into a single generic impl that narrows with a helper type so inference sticks. e.g.:

```ts
export function createClient<T = any>(opts: { auth?: string } & (T extends unknown ? { _type?: T } : {})) {
  // impl
}
```

Jordan P: or force callers to pass type arg explicitly if inference is fragile: "createClient<MyShape>({})". Ugly, but effective.

Anya W: FYI auth/retry also changed behavior: edge fetch polyfill drops keepalive semantics so our auth-refresh retry logic timed out in the sample. We should document difference and provide recommended retry hook for edge.

Sasha L: good catch. For edge recommend using AbortController and shorter timeouts + idempotency guard. We'll add a note in devex samples.

Anya W: action items:
- Matt: add ESM-only export path for dist/edge and verify package.exports mapping.
- Jordan: push a tiny SDK PR collapsing overloads or adding an explicit generic overload comment.
- Sasha: update sample tsconfig + add notes about edge fetch auth/retry semantics.

Matt R: starting a canary deploy for the sample changes now. tagging deploy-bot. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for sample-app-edge (canary-1793456789). Watch logs: https://deploys.internal/sample-app-edge/canary-1793456789

Anya W: thanks team. will follow up if the customer still sees the create() error. :thumbsup:

Matt R: if it persists, please paste the compiled bundle snippet (the function export) — that'll tell us whether interop shim is the culprit.

Jordan P: also add a tiny test in CI: run a quick esbuild build and `node --experimental-loader` or edge-like runtime smoke test to catch this earlier.

Sasha L: filing the DX docs PR now.

Anya W: perfect. closing the loop once canary proves green.
